event.title: SFSCON'26 - 'DMA Interoperability: What It Means for Free Software' in Bolzano, Italy in Bolzano, Italy

body.p: The EU Digital Markets Act (DMA) promises open digital markets by forcing gatekeepers like Apple and Google to grant “free and effective access to hardware and software features”, a direct opening for Free Software developers to build real alternatives. But two years into implementation, the gap between the law’s promise and what developers actually experience on the ground is striking.

How is interoperability actually being granted, and on what terms? While Apple’s public tracker lists nearly fifty interoperability requests, the real story lies in what gets denied, delayed, or buried in conditions that lock out Free Software projects.

This talk with Lucas Lasota and Dario Presutti presents what the FSFE has learned from two years of monitoring DMA implementation from a Free Software perspective. We will share findings from our developer survey, walk through Apple’s and Google’s gatekeeping practices, and explain what the FSFE is doing , including in court, to push back.
The talk will be in English and it will take place in the Seminar 4.
